newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady, much goes East for profit.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady, much goes East for profit.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady on Friday with much material heading east for profits.
Gas oil looked fairly balanced with Asian demand still pulling material out of the region, limiting the development of significant length.
Russian material continues to attract strong premiums, particuarly for large cargoes that can be worked eastwards. Traders said premiums were put around high cif quotes +$2-3.
Demand for non Russian 0.2 percent heating oil was also perky and combination cargoes with jet kerosene into France should be able to attract high fob quotes +$2.50-3.
Solo gas oil cargo premiums were lower at high fob quotes +$1.50-2, traders said.
There was understood to be some French interest for diesel which attracted premiums of high EN590 fob quotes +$2-3.
Gasoline was steady to slightly weaker in a balanced market. Most traders expected an uneventful market in the run-up to Easter with many players having covered needs well ahead.
Local demand remained fairly subdued, players said, but a high level of turnarounds countered the bullish effects of this.
Naphtha remained fairly tight with demand from the East draining supply.
Shipbrokers said Stasco had fixed a 27,500 tonne vessel out of Alexandria to South Korea loading April 8.

Fuel oil markets were subdued and prices stable. The flow of high sulphur material to the east and Italian refinery maintenance programmes limited supply in weeks ahead was seen keeping prices steady.

Talk of Romania's return to the fuel oil market also leant a bullish note. "If there were cargoes around you would think they'd get a decent price," said one trader. Higher U.S. prices meant low sulphur cargoes no longer overhung the Med but demand was thin and supplies of cheap material ample in NWE.
